_readme: Seven kinds of activity are available. Set "type" to one of:
mcq      multiple choice          questions[] with prompt, options[], answer, explanation
reading  passage + questions      passage[], passageTitle, then questions[] as for mcq
gap      fill in the blank        questions[] with sentence (use ____ for the space),
answer (a word, or a list of acceptable words), hint
order    put parts in order       questions[] with prompt, parts[] IN THE CORRECT ORDER
(the website shuffles them for the student)
match    match word to meaning    pairs[] with term and meaning
error    correct the mistake      questions[] with sentence, answer (the corrected
sentence, or a list of acceptable versions), explanation
'answer' in mcq and reading is the POSITION of the correct option, counting
from 0. So 0 is the first option, 1 the second, 2 the third, 3 the fourth.
'page' tells site search which page the activity lives on.
Every activity automatically gets instructions, immediate feedback, a score
and a 'Start again' button. Nothing a student types is stored or sent anywhere.
After editing this file, run build.cmd.

activities.title: Tenses: choosing the right form
activities.description: Ten questions on the tenses most often tested at Ordinary Level.
activities.keywords: tenses present past perfect continuous grammar quiz

questions.prompt: Nimal ____ to school every day.
questions.explanation: The simple present is used for a habit. With he, she or it, the verb takes -s: Nimal goes.

questions.prompt: Look! The bus ____ .
questions.explanation: The present continuous describes something happening at this moment. The word Look! tells you it is happening now.

questions.prompt: I ____ my homework already, so I can play now.
questions.explanation: The present perfect joins a past action to the present. The word already is a common signal for it.

questions.prompt: While I ____ , the telephone rang.
questions.explanation: Use the past continuous for the longer action that was already going on, and the simple past for the shorter action that interrupted it.

questions.prompt: She ____ in Kandy since 2015.
questions.explanation: Since names a starting point in the past and the situation continues, so the present perfect is used.

questions.prompt: We ____ the museum last Friday.
questions.explanation: Last Friday is a finished time, so the simple past is correct. Do not use the present perfect with a finished time expression.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film ____ .
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows which of two past actions happened first. The film started before you arrived.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ the match.
questions.explanation: In the first conditional the if-clause uses the simple present and the main clause uses will.

questions.prompt: The results ____ next week.
questions.explanation: The results do not announce anything; something is done to them, so the passive will be announced is needed.

questions.prompt: He ____ television when his father came home.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes the action in progress; the simple past came describes the shorter action that broke into it.

activities.title: Prepositions: in, on, at and the rest
activities.description: Eight questions on prepositions of time, place and movement.
activities.keywords: prepositions in on at grammar quiz

questions.prompt: The examination begins ____ 8.30 in the morning.
questions.explanation: Use at with a clock time: at 8.30, at noon, at midnight.

questions.prompt: My birthday is ____ May.
questions.explanation: Use in with months, seasons and years: in May, in December, in 2026.

questions.prompt: We have a test ____ Monday.
questions.explanation: Use on with days and dates: on Monday, on 15 March.

questions.prompt: She is very good ____ mathematics.
questions.explanation: Good at is a fixed pairing. We say good at a subject or a skill.

questions.prompt: Please listen ____ the instructions carefully.
questions.explanation: Listen is followed by to when there is an object: listen to the teacher, listen to music.

questions.prompt: The book is ____ the shelf.
questions.explanation: Use on for a surface. The shelf is a flat surface, so the book rests on it.

questions.prompt: He has been waiting ____ two hours.
questions.explanation: Use for with a length of time (for two hours) and since with a starting point (since ten o'clock).

questions.prompt: I apologised ____ being late.
questions.explanation: Apologise for is the usual pairing: apologise for a mistake, apologise for being late.

activities.title: Articles: a, an and the
activities.description: Type the missing article in each space.
activities.keywords: articles a an the fill in the blank

questions.sentence: My father is ____ engineer.
questions.hint: The next word begins with a vowel sound.
questions.explanation: Use an before a vowel sound: an engineer, an hour, an umbrella.

questions.sentence: She bought ____ new bicycle yesterday.
questions.explanation: Use a before a consonant sound, and when the thing is mentioned for the first time.

questions.sentence: ____ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: Use the before something there is only one of, such as the sun, the moon and the sky.

questions.sentence: I waited for ____ hour at the bus stand.
questions.hint: Listen to the sound, not the letter.
questions.explanation: Hour begins with the letter h, but the h is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound and takes an.

questions.sentence: He is ____ most careful student in the class.
questions.explanation: Superlatives take the: the most careful, the best, the tallest.

questions.sentence: We saw ____ elephant near the tank.
questions.explanation: Elephant begins with a vowel sound, so an is used.

questions.sentence: Colombo is ____ capital of Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: There is only one capital, so the is used.

questions.sentence: Would you like ____ cup of tea?
questions.explanation: One of several cups, mentioned for the first time, so a is correct.

activities.title: Verb forms: putting the verb in the right shape
activities.description: Write the correct form of the verb given in brackets.
activities.keywords: verb forms tenses fill in the blank practice

questions.sentence: The children ____ (play) in the garden now.
questions.explanation: The word now signals the present continuous: are playing.

questions.sentence: Water ____ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: A general truth takes the simple present. With water (it), the verb takes -s.

questions.sentence: I ____ (not see) him since Tuesday.
questions.explanation: Since points to a starting time and the situation continues, so the present perfect is used.

questions.sentence: They ____ (finish) the work before the rain started.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows the action that happened first of two past actions.

questions.sentence: The letter ____ (write) by the principal.
questions.explanation: The letter did not write anything, so the passive is needed: was written by the principal.

questions.sentence: She enjoys ____ (read) detective stories.
questions.explanation: After enjoy, the verb takes the -ing form: enjoy reading, enjoy swimming.

activities.title: Sentence ordering: building a correct sentence
activities.description: Put the parts in the right order to make a correct English sentence.
activities.keywords: sentence order word order syntax activity

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: English usually follows subject, verb, object or place, then time.

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: Already comes between the auxiliary verb has and the main verb informed.

questions.prompt: Make a correct question:
questions.explanation: Question word, then auxiliary, then subject, then the rest of the verb.

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: A sentence that begins with although needs a complete main clause after the comma.

questions.prompt: Make a correct sentence:
questions.explanation: In the first conditional the if-clause comes first, followed by a comma and the will-clause.

activities.description: Ten useful words that appear often in reading passages and in daily life.

costing a lot of money

activities.title: Literary terms: match the term to its meaning
activities.description: The terms students are most often asked to name and explain in Literature answers.
activities.keywords: literary terms simile metaphor imagery matching literature

pairs.meaning: a comparison of two different things using like or as
a comparison that speaks of one thing as though it actually were another
giving human qualities or actions to something that is not human
language that appeals to the senses and creates a picture in the mind
the repetition of the same consonant sound at the start of nearby words
a contrast between what is said or expected and what is actually the case
an object or action that stands for a larger idea beyond itself
a speech in which a character alone on stage reveals their thoughts
a group of lines in a poem, separated from other groups
a central idea about life that a work explores

activities.title: Reading comprehension: The village library
activities.description: Read the passage, then answer the six questions. This is the kind of passage used in Paper I.
passage: For many years the small village of Weliketiya had no library of its own. The nearest one was in the town, eleven kilometres away, and the bus that went there ran only twice a day. Children who wanted a book to read outside their school textbooks had to depend on the few volumes their teachers were able to lend them.

In 2019 a retired postmaster named Mr Alwis offered the front room of his house to the village. He had a large table, four chairs and, most importantly, patience. Villagers were asked to give any books they could spare. Within three months more than six hundred books had been collected, and the room was opened every evening from four o'clock until seven.

The library was not run by anybody official. Mr Alwis kept a simple notebook in which borrowers wrote their name, the title of the book and the date. There were no fines. If a book came back late, he said nothing; if it did not come back at all, he wrote the title on a separate page and hoped that one day it would return. Surprisingly, most books did.

What changed the village was not the number of books but the habit. Children who had never owned a story book began to read one every week. Parents who had left school early came in the evenings and borrowed simple books in English. Two of the older students began reading aloud to the youngest children on Saturday mornings, and that arrangement continues today.

questions.prompt: Before 2019, why was it difficult for the children of Weliketiya to borrow books?
options: The village library was closed for repairs.
The nearest library was far away and the bus was infrequent.
The children were not allowed to join the town library.
Their teachers refused to lend them books.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the nearest library was eleven kilometres away and the bus ran only twice a day.

questions.prompt: What did Mr Alwis give to the village?
options: Six hundred books from his own collection
Money to build a library building
The front room of his house, and his time
A bus service to the town library
questions.explanation: He offered the front room of his house, together with a table, chairs and patience. The books came from the villagers.

questions.prompt: How were the books collected?
options: They were bought with money raised in the village.
They were sent by the town library.
Villagers gave books they could spare.
The school donated its old textbooks.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph states that villagers were asked to give any books they could spare.

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about Mr Alwis's way of running the library?
options: It was strict and carefully controlled.
It was unpopular with the villagers.
questions.explanation: There were no fines, records were kept in a simple notebook, and late books were met with silence. This shows a trusting, informal manner.

questions.prompt: According to the last paragraph, what mattered most about the library?
options: The money it saved the village
The fact that it was free
questions.explanation: The writer says plainly that what changed the village was not the number of books but the habit.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means 'happening or existing without an official arrangement'?
questions.explanation: Informal is the word that matches this meaning. The passage tells us the library was not run by anybody official.

activities.title: Literature: naming the technique
activities.description: Eight questions asking you to name the technique a writer has used. Naming the technique correctly is the first step in every good Literature answer.
activities.keywords: literary techniques simile metaphor quiz literature

questions.prompt: 'The classroom was as quiet as a temple at dawn.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The comparison uses the word as, so it is a simile. A metaphor would say the classroom was a temple.

questions.prompt: 'The wind pushed open the door and walked into the room.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human actions of pushing and walking, so this is personification.

questions.prompt: 'Silent shadows slipped across the sand.' Which technique is most obvious?
questions.explanation: The s sound is repeated at the start of several nearby words, which is alliteration.

questions.prompt: A fire officer's own house burns down. In literary terms this is an example of:
questions.explanation: There is a sharp contrast between what we would expect and what actually happens, which is irony.

questions.prompt: A character alone on stage speaks his private thoughts aloud to the audience. This is a:
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is spoken by a character who is alone, revealing thoughts the other characters do not hear.

questions.prompt: 'Her hands were rough maps of forty harvests.' Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: The hands are spoken of as though they actually were maps, with no like or as, so it is a metaphor.

questions.prompt: In a story, a broken watch that the father keeps for thirty years stands for time that cannot be recovered. The watch is being used as a:
questions.explanation: An object that stands for a larger idea beyond itself is a symbol.

questions.prompt: Which of these best defines a theme?
options: The order in which events happen
The place where the story is set
A central idea about life that the work explores
questions.explanation: A theme is an idea about life, such as loss, duty or the cost of ambition. The order of events is plot; the place is setting; the person telling it is the narrator.

activities.title: Error correction: find the mistake and put it right
activities.description: Each sentence has one mistake. Rewrite the whole sentence correctly.
activities.keywords: error correction common mistakes grammar editing

questions.sentence: She don't like cold weather.
answer: She does not like cold weather
questions.explanation: With he, she or it, the negative is doesn't, not don't.

questions.sentence: I am living here since 2018.
answer: I have been living here since 2018
questions.explanation: Since with a continuing situation needs the present perfect, not the present continuous.

questions.sentence: He is more taller than his brother.
answer: He is taller than his brother
questions.explanation: Do not use more together with an -er comparative. Taller is already the comparative form.

questions.sentence: The informations you gave me were useful.
answer: The information you gave me was useful
The information you gave me was very useful
questions.explanation: Information is uncountable. It has no plural and takes a singular verb.

questions.sentence: We discussed about the problem yesterday.
questions.explanation: Discuss is followed directly by its object. Do not add about.

questions.sentence: Every students must bring a pen.
answer: Every student must bring a pen
questions.explanation: Every is followed by a singular noun: every student, every day, every question.

questions.sentence: He asked me where do I live.
answer: He asked me where I live
He asked me where I lived
questions.explanation: In reported questions the word order returns to normal statement order, and do is dropped.

questions.sentence: I look forward to hear from you.
answer: I look forward to hearing from you
questions.explanation: In look forward to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb after it takes the -ing form.
